items.title: Marty Morell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 24, 2017
items.q: And also Rocky White, the drummer, Duke Ellington himself hired Rocky, right?

ctx.x: Well the thing is that that band is actually from the original times when Duke started it, right, so it would go along and when somebody died, that position got filled, right? So they kept everything going. You know Duke passed and Mercer took over, and some of

the guys that had worked with Duke still stayed in the band so it was kind of always passing the flag to the next person. So there was a certain way to play in that band and that’s what — if you could do that then you got the gig, that type of thing. Right? So I’m honored to have been part of that Ellington legacy even though – actually I worked with Barry Lee Hall. Barry Lee Hall unfortunately passed away a few years ago. He was a trumpet player and he worked with Ellington. All right? So he was the last…
That’s right. There’s this – Ellington never fired anyone I guess, at least that’s what I’ve read.
